text:
alex: FYI — We're seeing a customer escalation (acct: acme-corp) that started ~2026-03-14T09:12Z. They reported spikes of 429s and then a flurry of 500s. I dug in and it looks like our rate limiter stopped refilling tokens for a subset of API keys after a short burst.

maya: acme pinged support at 09:11 complaining timed out requests and intermittent 429s. Repro steps they gave: they hit /v1/completions w/ ~300 RPS for ~30s then their throughput dropped to nothing. Said it recovered after ~2h.

joel: I can reproduce locally. Quick summary of the bug: token_bucket.refill() uses last_refill_ts from an in-memory map keyed by key+region. When global_overflow flag flips (we set it for emergency throttles), the refill path skips updating last_refill_ts due to an early return. That leaves last_refill_ts stale and subsequent refill calculations yield negative deltas, so bucket never gains tokens again.

joel: Repro steps I used (local service run):
```bash
# simulate burst, then request after refill window
for i in {1..350}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "X-API-Key: test-acme" http://localhost:8080/v1/completions & done
sleep 3
curl -v -H "X-API-Key: test-acme" http://localhost:8080/v1/completions
```
Response: then we see 429s until manual reset.

alex: Log snippets (redacted):
```
[09:10:23] rate_limiter: key=test-acme bucket_tokens=0 last_refill_ts=1621412345
[09:10:24] rate_limiter: global_overflow=true -> short-circuit return
[09:12:30] rate_limiter: request denied 429 key=test-acme tokens=0
```
Notice last_refill_ts never updated after overflow flip.

ratebot: ALERT: rate_limiter.high_429s for host inference-prod-17 — 182 incidents in 5m. Ticket: #INC-2026-498 (automated)

emma: What mitigations did we apply? Are we rolling back config or patching code? Acme is asking for timeline and RCA.

alex: Immediate mitigation I pushed at 09:24:
- toggled config: limiter.global_overflow=false for affected region (allowed refill path to resume)
- increased per-key burst window temporarily: limiter.defaults.max_burst=2000 -> reduces chance of hitting zero on short bursts
This allowed most keys to recover within ~8-10 minutes. Not ideal but buys time for patch.

joel: I prepared a hotfix PR to ensure refill() always updates last_refill_ts before any early returns and to make global_overflow transient-only (don't skip bookkeeping). Also added unit tests that simulate overflow transitions. Patch: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/PR/4721 (link is internal). Test plan attached in PR.

maya: Customer update drafted: "We identified an internal rate-limiter edge case where a transient emergency throttle prevented token refills for some keys after a burst. We applied a configuration change to allow automatic refills and are rolling a code patch to permanently fix the logic. We're also adding extra observability and a runbook. ETA for full fix: 2 hrs." Anyone object?

emma: Let's add that we will credit them for the downtime window as part of support remediation. Also, ensure Legal/CS are looped if they threaten SLA credits.

alex: Post-incident followups we agreed on: 
- ship hotfix PR and roll to prod canary within 30m
- add synthetic test: isolated overflow-toggle + burst scenario against a canary deployment
- add a dashboard for "tokens_refill_rate" per-key with alert when refill rate == 0 for >2m and requests > 50/min
- add an automatic fallback: if refill_rate==0 then switch to redis-based fallback token bucket for that key for 10m (less chance of in-memory metadata corruption)
- revise defaults: increase conservative burst tolerance for tenant-heavy endpoints

joel: Notes on rollout: hotfix is small; canary on 10% of traffic for 20m w/ immediate rollback on >1% increase in 5xx or 429s. I'm scheduling the canary at 10:05 UTC.

ratebot: DEPLOY: infra/rate-limiter v1.3.2 started canary on inference-prod-17 at 10:06:12 UTC. Canary traffic=10%.

alex: Monitoring after canary: within 6 minutes tokens_refill_rate normalized and 429 counts dropped to baseline. Rolling to 100% now.

maya: Customer confirmed recovery at 10:20 and asked for postmortem + timeline. I'm drafting the postmortem and will ask for input on timeline accuracy.

emma: Action owners: joel -> fix + unit tests + canary (PR owner). alex -> deploy config guardrails and add dashboard alerts. maya -> customer comms + credits coordination. I'll own the postmortem writeup and follow-up with Legal on SLA.

joel: Added to PR: a regression test that simulates overflow flip mid-burst and asserts bucket tokens increase after next refill window. Also logging improvements to print both last_refill_ts and computed_refill_delta.

alex: Quick decision: we should not rely solely on in-memory last_refill_ts for any key that can be toggled by global flags. Put a small periodic compaction job that normalizes/repairs stale metadata every 5 minutes. I'll file a ticket.

maya: Thanks — pushing customer note now. I'll attach the canary/rollout timeline and proposed credit.

emma: Sounds good. Once PR merges and is fully rolled, we'll close the incident. Please add any follow-up tasks to the incident doc.

alex: Closing note: root cause = logic path in refill() that returned early on global_overflow and skipped bookkeeping. Contributing factor = conservative defaults that make tokens hit zero quickly during bursts.

maya: Adding final customer-facing language: "root cause was an internal limiter edge-case; fixed in code; added monitoring and will provide credit details." Posting now. :white_check_mark:

joel: PR merged at 10:32, full rollout completed 10:40, monitoring shows stable.

emma: Thanks everyone. Postmortem draft link: https://docs.internal/redwood/incidents/INC-2026-498/postmortem (internal). I'll review and send to ops.
